Theme 088 · Art movements & eras

Op Art Illusion

Bridget Riley and Victor Vasarely's optical art turned into a monitoring metaphor: healthy data is a perfectly regular pattern that vibrates on the beat, and an anomaly is a warp in the field your eye finds before your brain does. Ink-on-paper stripes, teal concentric rings and one coral compression.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Riley wave field — 52 sine-modulated ink stripes, 11 px, as visual overload
  • Vasarely tunnel — offset concentric teal/paper rings that pull toward the mark
  • Checker field — regular squares standing for healthy metrics
  • Warp zone — column compression where squares turn coral — the anomaly
  • Ink-bordered card — 8 px ink frame holding type calmly on top of the pattern
  • Calm stripes — evenly spaced teal bars for the resolved end state

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Phase shimmer — wave phase += 0.35 rad per 8th note, stepped (no easing) so the vibration locks to 120 BPM
  • Warp squeeze — column widths animate to the Gaussian compression, sine.inOut 1 s (2 beats); relax with elastic.out after the human clicks
  • Tunnel pull — ring scale 1→1.25 with expo.in 0.5 s into the drop, then hard cut to the settled frame

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

It dramatises the core promise — Pulse sees the break in the pattern — with pure perception, no UI needed, and it is a scroll-stopper in a feed. Risk: strong moiré can shimmer badly after video compression and cause discomfort; keep stripes ≥ 10 px, avoid flicker faster than 3 Hz and always rest text on a solid card.

Adapt to your product: Use the regular pattern for 'normal' in your domain (requests, transactions, builds) and warp it where your product catches something. Replace the evidence card with your own alert UI.

References: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Op_art — optical-art techniques: line vibration, figure-ground, colour contrast · https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridget_Riley — Current (1964), Movement in Squares (1961)
